title: Полгода на кухне и текучка кадров  (Six Months in the Kitchen and Staff Turnover)

segments.t: Welcome to Kukhnya Season 2, Episode 12. Max looks back on the six months he has spent working at Claude Monet, recalling all the rookies who could not handle the heat and how people constantly come and go in the restaurant world.
Ты что тут делаешь с рыбой?
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
'That I have been working here.' Max follows up openly in the exchange and reaches for the Russian word "rabotayu" ("work", built from "rabotat") right at the center of the line.
'Over those six months.' Discussing the six months at once, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'I ordered zucchini.' Max chimes in frankly during the talk, letting the remark speak for itself.
'Do you call this zucchini?' Discussing the zucchini around Max, Barinov uses "po-tvoyemu" ("wife", from "po-tvoiy") to make the point stick.
'Guys, I forgot to update the eighty-six list.' Discussing the list beside Barinov, Max chooses "stop-list" ("86'd list") so Barinov gets the point right away.
'This is your station now.' Barinov replies wryly in this moment, leaving no doubt about where he stands.
Ты что тут делаешь с рыбой?
'What are you doing here with the fish?' Highlighting the fish during the talk, Max leans on "delayesh" ("are you doing", a form of "delat") to give the remark its edge.
'Who fillets a fish like that?' Touching on a fish before Max, Barinov puts the question word "kto" right at the start so Max hears the focus immediately.
'What do you think you are doing?' Max wonders firmly to see how Barinov will answer on the spot.
'Who fillets fish like that?' Bringing up the fish in this beat, Barinov centers the thought on "razdelyvayet" ("to butcher", from "razdelyvat") without wasting a word.
'I am asking you!' Opening up directly right here, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Yet there are plenty of people eager to get hired too.' Barinov answers frankly toward Max, before Max can change the subject.
'Some leave, and others arrive.' Max steps in warmly around Barinov and brings in "ukhodyat" ("are leaving", from "ukhodit") as the key Russian word here.
Ты что тут делаешь с рыбой?
That wraps up this scene as max reflects on the many cooks who have come and gone during his six months at Claude Monet as Lyova struggles to run the kitchen alone. Until next time!
